changelog: SD-card trouble detection (v35). The 2026 SD-card failure incidents were only ever caught by the card fully dying and the device boot-looping, after which the update mechanism could not run and the card was unreadable -- so this version's goal is to detect the card going bad and email someone BEFORE that point. Runs on every HA start: (1) boot events are recorded to /config/.cytech_boot_events and a restart storm (5+ HA starts in 24h) is flagged from it, (2) cytech_check_sdcard.sh greps the host kernel journal (via the SSH addon container, which sees host logs) for mmc/I-O/CRC/ext4 error signatures and counts host boots started today, and (3) cytech_canary.sh writes and reads back an 8 MB test file on the data partition to exercise the write path. Each writes a small JSON result file under /config that a new command_line sensor exposes (sensor.cytech_sdcard_result / sensor.cytech_canary_result / sensor.cytech_boot_result, state OK/FAIL/SKIP or RESTART_STORM). On any FAIL/RESTART_STORM an automation emails the alert (smtp notify, send-only ucmapi@cytech.biz account) to Cytech support, to the device owner, or to both -- chosen by the user via input_select.cytech_alert_destination, with the choice surfaced on the Config Files dashboard's new System Health section. The owner's SMTP password is NEVER in this repo or the golden image: the device keeps it in its existing /config/.cytech_secrets and ensure_email_secrets() in first_boot.sh feeds it into secrets.yaml at setup (no-op until CY_SMTP_PASS exists, so upgrading devices just stay quiet -- no restart, no email until the owner walks the one-time setup step). Physical after-effect on the card: one 8 MB file per start (~3 GB/year at one boot/day; HA itself writes 100s of MB/day -- both deliberately cheap and both, unlike the failure modes being detected, self-healing). If a check cannot run at all (SSH addon down, tools missing) it reports SKIP rather than disturbing startup. Note: hardware-SMTP and recursive checking are deliberately NOT included -- this detects the card going bad, not a dead device (a device that cannot even boot cannot email from inside HA; that case is still caught by the failing to check in, i.e. no more boot events).
